title: Score the dual, sort the houses, and run the KKT checklist
brief: Compute a table of pairwise similarities, score points and the dual objective from the pushes alone, sort every house into its group, and compute the number that says how badly a set of pushes breaks the best-road picture.
hints: The linear Gram matrix is X @ X.T. The RBF kernel needs squared distances: ||a - b||^2 = ||a||^2 + ||b||^2 - 2 a.b. Clip them at 0 before you call exp, because the diagonal can come out as -1e-16.
dual_scores is f = (alpha * y) @ K + b, and dual_objective is alpha.sum() - 0.5 * v @ K @ v with v = alpha * y. Dropping the labels in v is the usual mistake.
A stored push of 1e-16 is zero for every practical purpose. Compare alpha with tol (alpha <= tol, alpha >= C - tol), never with ==.
margin_groups returns 0 for 'no push', 1 for 'free' (0 < alpha < C), and 2 for 'capped'. Start from np.ones(n, dtype=int) and overwrite the two ends.
Slack is max(0, 1 - y f), the same shortfall as the hinge loss. It is the negative of g_i = y_i f_i - 1, clipped at 0.
kkt_violation: build g = y * f - 1 with dual_scores, then per group take max(0, -g) for group 0, abs(g) for group 1, and max(0, g) for group 2. Return the largest.
